title: openai-compat: map tool schemas + implement tool_choice semantics + format tool messages
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling so that tools provided by customers or the Redwood model catalog are faithfully represented to OpenAI-style clients. This PR addresses three gaps identified in compatibility testing: 1) missing mapping from Redwood tool schemas (protobuf/JSON Schema variants) to OpenAI-style `parameters` schemas, 2) incorrect handling of the `tool_choice` message returned by models (we previously used a non-standard envelope), and 3) inconsistent formatting of tool-invocation messages in the conversation stream which breaks some downstream SDKs.
Summary of changes:
- Add schema mapper that converts Redwood tool schema variants to OpenAI-compatible `parameters` JSON Schema (handles typed enums, nested objects, required fields, and examples).
- Implement `tool_choice` semantics per OpenAI spec: when model returns a `tool_choice`, platform emits a single assistant message with role=assistant and content="" plus a separate `tool` metadata object for the selected tool; previously we emitted a custom system message which caused SDKs to ignore the choice.
- Normalize tool invocation messages in streaming: tool.name and tool.arguments are emitted as a structured JSON blob in a single delta chunk, followed by an explicit end-of-tool-call marker. This improves compatibility with streaming-aware clients.
- Add compatibility tests and end-to-end integration tests against the OpenAI compatibility harness.
Migration notes and developer guidance:
- Existing clients that relied on the old envelope for tool_choice must update to read the new assistant message + tool metadata model. The Redwood SDKs (this repo) have been updated to surface the same object shapes as the upstream OpenAI SDKs; see redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript packages in this PR for examples.
- Tool schema mapping tries to preserve field descriptions and examples when possible; if mapping fails we fall back to a permissive object schema to avoid blocking.
Implementation details:
- New module redwood/openai_compat/tool_schema_mapper.py implements a deterministic mapping pipeline with unit tests for common patterns (primitives, arrays, enums, nested objects, oneOf/anyOf -> anyOf fallback documented).
- Runtime changes in the inference event streamer (redwood/runtime/streaming/openai_compat_streamer.py): integrate mapper output into model catalog tool descriptors and emit the `tool_choice` formatted assistant+tool pair during stream assembly.
- SDK updates: redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript updated to parse and surface tool_choice and tool invocation deltas in the same shape as official OpenAI SDKs; added backward-compat shims with warnings for one release.
- Tests: added unit tests for mapping, serializer tests for streaming deltas, and an integration test that runs the OpenAI compatibility harness end-to-end using a local test model returning tool_choice.
Risk and mitigations:
- Backwards compatibility: toggled behind feature flag `openai_compat.tool_choice_v2` for 2 weeks to monitor errors in production.
- Edge cases: complex oneOf schemas are flattened to an anyOf-compatible representation and documented; warnings are emitted in logs so customers can provide explicit schema overrides.
- Performance: mapping is cached per-tool descriptor in the model catalog to avoid per-request cost.
Release notes:
- Implements OpenAI-style tool schema mapping and tool_choice semantics; updates SDKs to match OpenAI shapes; streaming tool invocation messages are normalized; feature-flagged rollout.
Checklists:
- [x] Schema mapping implementation + unit tests
- [x] Streamer integration + streaming tests
- [x] SDK parsing/compat shims + examples
- [x] Integration test against OpenAI compat harness
- [x] Docs and migration notes added to redwood-docs/compat/openai-tool-calling.md
commits_summary: feat(openai-compat): add tool schema mapper and mapping tests
fix(streaming): emit tool invocation as structured delta with end marker
feat(sdk): parse tool_choice in python and typescript SDKs
chore(tests): add openai-compat integration test harness job
docs: add migration guide for tool calling
review_comments: Marco Chen: Nice work, this addresses a lot of the mismatch we saw in the compat tests. Two asks: 1) add a note about oneOf->anyOf fallback in the docs, and 2) can we emit a specific warning metric when mapping falls back?
Author (Aisha): Added docs note and emitted openai_compat.schema_mapping.fallback metric; see redwood/openai_compat/tool_schema_mapper.py#L210
Riley Thompson: The streamer changes look good but I want to see an E2E test that validates streaming deltas order — added a test request in comments.
Author (Aisha): Added tests/openai_compat/test_streaming_tool_invocation.py which asserts delta ordering and end-of-tool-call marker in the stream.
Priya Kapoor: SDK parsing looks fine. Please add a deprecation warning for the old envelope in the next patch release.
Author (Aisha): Added deprecation warnings and feature flag gating to SDK shims; will follow up with a short deprecation RFC.
CI: Integration job flaked twice on first run (timeout on harness). Re-ran and all checks passed.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag openai_compat.tool_choice_v2 is enabled on staging and will be rolled to prod by ops on 2024-10-20 if no regressions are observed.
When enabling in prod, ensure feature flag rollout is gradual (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and dashboards track openai_compat.schema_mapping.fallback and openai_compat.tool_choice_errors.
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: tool schema mapping, tool_choice semantics, streaming tool invocation normalization. SDKs updated; migration guide available in docs.
